claim: REQ-504's edge case makes an unverified, and in fact FALSE, ground-truth claim about the existing codebase's behavior, and as a direct consequence REQ-504/REQ-505 leave a real, unaddressed bypass path by which a model can trivially defeat the ENTIRE always-act mechanism even after the sleep TOOL is correctly withheld from the outbound schema. REQ-504's edge case (behavioral-spec.md:222-225) states: 'A model response that nonetheless attempts slot: "sleep" or any slot outside the enum (a spec/tool-contract violation by the model, not the harness -- the schema truly does not offer it) is rejected THE SAME WAY AN INVALID ENUM VALUE IS ALREADY REJECTED TODAY, and is treated as a no-tool-call outcome for REQ-505's purposes.' I directly read runtime/loop/index.mjs's full wake-loop (lines 382-421) and there is NO existing enum-validation step anywhere in the real code: after `parseToolCall(rawResponse)` returns a non-null `{slot, args}` (which it does for ANY object with a `function.name` or a `slot` field in its JSON args -- see runtime/loop/parse-tool-call.mjs:41, `const slot = parsed.slot ?? toolCall.function.name`, with zero cross-check against which tools were actually offered in the request), index.mjs unconditionally executes `if (slot === 'sleep') { ...write a kind:'narrate' ledger line...sleepSecs(sleepS);return; }` at index.mjs:403-416 -- purely a STRING equality check on `slot`, with no reference to `ctx.alwaysActEngaged`, `ctx.alwaysActMenu`, or whether SLEEP_TOOL was actually present in the request's `tools` array. Consequently, if the model emits `run_skill({slot:"sleep"})` (a perfectly legal `run_skill` call whose `args.slot` string is simply the literal text "sleep" -- not the withheld SLEEP_TOOL function at all), OR directly names a tool_call function "sleep" despite that name being absent from the offered schema (a well-documented behavior of weak/free models, which is EXACTLY why this same codebase already ships a multi-strategy scavenge/repair parser in parse-tool-call.mjs for models that don't reliably follow structured tool-calling formats, and why ANICCA_FREE_MODEL=free/gpt-oss-120b is this loop's own documented safety-floor default model), index.mjs's existing, UNMODIFIED line 403 check will still match and silently produce the exact idle/no-op narrate-and-sleep outcome this entire feature exists to structurally forbid (doctrine §0: 'idle/WAIT is a failure signal ... skip は malware だ'). Neither the Purity Boundary Map (verification-architecture.md:51-78) nor any REQ (501-512) lists index.mjs:403's `if (slot === 'sleep')` branch as a location requiring modification -- the spec's own list of 'additively modified' index.mjs locations covers only the classify call-site gate (line 450) and the REQ-512 ledger appends, never this branch. This is therefore not merely an unverified citation but a concrete, unaddressed structural loophole that fully defeats REQ-504/505/506's core purpose.
evidence: behavioral-spec.md:222-225 (REQ-504 edge case's false claim, no supporting citation given) vs the REAL code: runtime/loop/index.mjs:402-416 (`if (slot === 'sleep') { ... }` -- unconditional string check, no enum/ctx cross-reference, confirmed unmodified by this spec's own Purity Boundary Map) and runtime/loop/parse-tool-call.mjs:26-60 (`parseToolCall` extracts `slot` from either the tool_call function name OR the JSON args' `slot` field, with zero validation against an offered-tools list) plus runtime/loop/parse-tool-call.mjs:106-138 (the existing scavenge/repair logic, present precisely because weak/free models do not reliably respect structured tool schemas -- corroborating that a stray 'sleep'-named call from a weak model is a realistic, not theoretical, risk for this exact harness).
required_fix: Add REQ-504/REQ-505 language (and a corresponding entry in the Purity Boundary Map's Effectful Shell list for index.mjs) that explicitly modifies index.mjs's existing `if (slot === 'sleep')` branch: when `ctx.alwaysActEngaged` is true, that branch MUST NOT be honored as a legitimate sleep -- either (a) reject it and route it into REQ-505's no-tool-call/reprompt handling (treating a stray slot:'sleep' identically to a genuinely no-tool-call response), or (b) treat it as an invalid `run_skill` pick outside the enum and route it into REQ-506's reroute handling with the model's chosen slot excluded. Add an explicit PROP (e.g. PROP-504c) asserting that when `ctx.alwaysActEngaged===true`, a parsed tool call of exactly `{slot:'sleep', args:{}}` (simulating a weak model ignoring the schema) is REJECTED by the ACTUAL `index.mjs` wake loop (not just absent from the pure tool-definitions helper) and never produces a `kind:'narrate'`/idle ledger line.
